goal.text: Yeah is an Emacs Lisp agent harness: the user's Emacs session is itself the runtime of the agent; every call to the model goes through gptel, every tool goes through the registry and the permission system, and the session log stays append-only

claims.subject: every file under lib/ byte-compiles without errors and without warnings
claims.falsifier: the byte-compilation of lib/ fails, or reports a warning

claims.subject: the agent loop is a finite state machine with exactly twelve states and twenty transitions: the machine can run one model turn and be asked again, and it can record a turn that failed
claims.falsifier: the state list or the transition table has a different length, a transition is missing, or the machine cannot return to the model
claims.control: sed -i 's/^    interrupted$/    completed-tmp/; s/^    completed$/    interrupted/; s/^    completed-tmp$/    completed/' lib/yeah-state.el

claims.subject: the session log is append-only: a record that has been written is never rewritten and never removed
claims.falsifier: an earlier record is missing from the file after a later append

claims.subject: compaction is a projection: the source records stay on disk and the compaction record joins them
claims.falsifier: a source record disappears from the log when the compaction runs

claims.subject: a tool call is refused when the number of arguments, or the type of one of them, does not match the tool's declared input
claims.falsifier: a call with the wrong number of arguments, or with an argument of the wrong type, is accepted

claims.subject: the permission system decides by the last matching rule, and asks when nothing matches
claims.falsifier: an earlier matching rule overrides a later one, or the default stops being ask
claims.control: sed -i 's/(setq last-match rule)/(unless last-match (setq last-match rule))/' lib/yeah-perm.el

claims.subject: the ACP dispatcher answers initialize, session/new, session/prompt and session/cancel, and refuses a method it does not know
claims.falsifier: one of the four methods is unrouted, or an unknown method is answered instead of refused

claims.subject: the emcp registry and schemas/emcp-v1.json name the same tools, and a duplicate id is refused
claims.falsifier: the registry and the schema name different tools, or a duplicate id is accepted

claims.subject: every tick's changes can be undone: an undo boundary is taken around the buffer or the file the tick touched
claims.falsifier: a change made inside the boundary is not recorded in the undo list

claims.subject: the gptel hooks are registered in exactly one module, lib/yeah-gptel.el, and nowhere else in lib/
claims.falsifier: a second module mentions a gptel hook variable

claims.subject: a sub-agent spawns a child session, waits for it, and a spawn past the depth limit is refused
claims.falsifier: the child session is not created, or the depth limit is not enforced

claims.subject: the Yeah shell keeps a bounded history of what was sent to it, and creates its REPL buffer
claims.falsifier: the history is unbounded, or the REPL buffer is not created

claims.subject: the tick, the permission system, the tool registry and the session log are wired into one loop: each is called from outside its own module
claims.falsifier: a module of the loop is called only from inside itself

claims.subject: the PTC sandbox refuses a form whose name is not whitelisted, and refuses code inside a whitelisted form that calls outside the whitelist
claims.falsifier: the sandbox executes code the model supplied, or accepts a form outside the whitelist

claims.subject: the model is called through the gptel hook surface and nowhere else: one function in one module is the whole of the transport
claims.falsifier: a second module calls the model directly, or the call site does not exist

claims.subject: the ACP agent speaks JSON-RPC over stdio: a client can open the process and exchange an initialize request and its answer
claims.falsifier: a client cannot exchange a JSON-RPC message with the agent over stdio

claims.subject: one turn asks the model, dispatches the tool calls the model asked for through the permission system and the registry, writes what happened into the log, and asks the model again until it asks for nothing
claims.falsifier: a tool call the model asked for is not dispatched, or is dispatched without the rules deciding, or the results do not reach the log

claims.subject: the tool calls of one answer of the model run together: a shared tool may run alongside the other shared tools, an exclusive tool runs alone, and the batch settles only when every call has settled
claims.falsifier: two shared calls of one answer run one after the other, an exclusive call runs while another is running, or the batch continues before its last call has settled

claims.subject: every step of a run is a typed record of the log: what the model asked, what the rules answered, what the tool did, and what the model said, and a record carries the fields its type declares
claims.falsifier: the log holds a record of an unknown type, a record whose fields are not the ones its type declares, or a step of the run that leaves no record
claims.control: sed -i 's/(unless (yeah-events--same-fields-p declared given)/(unless t (yeah-events--same-fields-p declared given)/' lib/yeah-events.el

claims.subject: the interface shows the run as it happens: the transcript, the tool calls in flight, the pending approval and the cost so far
claims.falsifier: the interface cannot show what the run is doing without reading the log

claims.subject: an approval is answered once, always or rejected, and a run without a human resolves the question by policy instead of failing
claims.falsifier: a run without a human dies on its first approval, or an answer given once is remembered forever

claims.subject: the context is compacted by a model call that keeps the tail, and the outputs of old tools are pruned separately
claims.falsifier: the context is compacted by a placeholder, or a long run grows without bound

claims.subject: sessions can be listed, resumed, branched and reverted, and every session reports what it cost in tokens and money
claims.falsifier: a session cannot be resumed, a branch loses the abandoned path, or the cost of a session is unknown

claims.subject: a failing call is retried with backoff, every tool has a timeout, a run has a deadline, and nothing waits in the main loop
claims.falsifier: a transient failure is not retried, a hanging tool has no timeout, or the main loop waits

claims.subject: the emacs tool namespace is served over stdio, and the tools it publishes are the ones the registry holds
claims.falsifier: a client cannot list or call the published tools, or the published set drifts from the registry

claims.subject: the same kernel runs attached to a session, in its own Emacs as a service, and in batch, and the placement changes nothing but the answer to a question
claims.falsifier: the kernel behaves differently depending on where it runs, or a run in a service cannot reach the buffers of a person

claims.subject: a sub-agent runs in its own session with its own context and its own permissions, and its result comes back to the parent
claims.falsifier: a sub-agent shares the parent context, or exceeds the depth limit, or its result is lost

claims.subject: the harness installs, serves and explains itself: an installation path, a server mode, and documentation written for a person
claims.falsifier: the harness cannot be installed, cannot be served, or can only be used by an agent that reads the source
